draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Badami! This red sandstone town used to be Vatapi, the capital of the Badami Chalukyas from 540 to 757. Its cave temples, cut right into the cliff above Agastya lake, are some of the earliest Hindu temples in the Deccan.
draft.hungryLine: Station Road has the easy picks, from cheap veg meals near the bus stand to tandoori chicken a little out of town, and wash it down with buttermilk or roadside tea.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Badami Cave Temples are a 7 min walk, and the Lower Shivalaya is just 5 minutes away. The museum is close too, and the 300 stairs up to the Shivalayas start right beside it.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Climb up to the Upper Shivalaya plateau for sunset over Badami, just get back down before the museum gate is locked at 6PM.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The Upper Shivalaya isn't actually a Shiva temple. Despite the name, it's a Vaishnava temple.

spots.name: Badami Cave Temples
spots.detail: 7 min walk · Four caves, the first one dug out by the Chalukyas around 550 AD

spots.name: Lower Shivalaya
spots.detail: 5 min walk · On the stair path up the hill, with the granaries and Upper Shivalaya above

spots.name: Bhutanatha Temple
spots.detail: 12 min walk · Sandstone shrines on the east side of the lake

tips.title: Time your sunset climb.
tips.body: The Upper Shivalaya plateau is great for sunset, but the metal gate at the museum is locked at 6PM.

tips.title: Check climbing gear carefully.
tips.body: You can hire ropes and quickdraws in town for the sandstone cliffs, but make sure the rope is still in good shape.

story.title: A lake in a ravine
story.body: Agastya lake was made by people around the 5th to 7th century, ringed by an earthen wall with stone steps. It's also called Vatapi lake, after the town's old name.

story.title: Chalukya capital
story.body: Vatapi was the royal capital of the Badami Chalukyas, who ruled much of Karnataka. The hill fort above town was their seat.

story.title: Caves in the cliff
story.body: The first cave temple, for Shiva, was carved around 550 AD. Two more for Vishnu and one with Jain carvings followed, and with Aihole they turned this river valley into a cradle of temple design.

story.title: Many rulers
story.body: The fort was changed again and again by the Vijayanagara Empire, the Bahmani and Adil Shahi sultans and Tipu Sultan before it fell into ruin.

story.title: Heritage city
story.body: The fort is now looked after by the Archaeological Survey of India, with a museum of recovered sculptures and inscriptions next door. Badami was picked as one of the heritage cities under the HRIDAY scheme.
